8. Leakage Problems — Detailed Troubleshooting
Manual
This document contains 7 separate troubleshooting topics. Each topic starts on a new page and is written as a
sequential procedure. User-level checks are separated from service-level diagnosis.
Model basis: Samsung's WA5471ABP/XAA support page lists the model-specific User Manual (version 4, modified May 3, 2016). The
technical information for the WA5471 series documents troubleshooting areas including water valves, inlet screens, hoses, water level
sensing, drain/spin, motor, PCB connections, and related service diagnosis. turn0search13I
Samsung WA5471ABP/XAA — Leakage Problems
Page 2

8.1. Water leaking from washer
What this means: Water leaking from washer is treated as the observed symptom or fault condition. Follow
the steps in order and stop when the cause is identified.
Step-by-step procedure

Step 1. Stop the washer and, if water is actively leaking, stop the water supply if it can be done safely.

Step 2. Do not touch electrical connections or plugs if water has reached them. Treat the situation as an electrical

safety hazard.

Step 3. Identify where the water first appears: inlet hose, drain hose, dispenser area, bottom of cabinet, or
tub/seal area.

Step 4. Inspect the accessible hose connections for looseness, damaged washers, cracks, or obvious
displacement.

Step 5. If a hose is visibly loose and can be safely reseated without opening the washer, correct the connection
and dry the surrounding area.

Step 6. Run a short supervised test only after the area is dry and there is no electrical hazard.

Step 7. If water originates from inside the cabinet, the bottom, or a tub/seal area, stop using the washer and
arrange service rather than opening the machine.
When to escalate: If the problem remains after the safe external checks, or if the washer shows repeated electrical,
sensor, control, motor, valve, pump, or lock faults, stop user troubleshooting and arrange qualified service.
Samsung WA5471ABP/XAA — Leakage Problems
Page 3

8.2. Water leaking from inlet hose
What this means: Water leaking from inlet hose is treated as the observed symptom or fault condition. Follow
the steps in order and stop when the cause is identified.
Step-by-step procedure

Step 1. Turn the washer off using the Power button and wait until the controls are no longer active before
inspecting external water connections.

Step 2. Confirm that the household water supply is available. Open the appropriate water faucet fully and check
that water can flow normally.

Step 3. Inspect the hot and cold inlet hoses along their full visible length. Make sure neither hose is sharply bent,
crushed, twisted, or trapped against the washer.

Step 4. Check both hose connections at the washer and at the water supply. Each connection should be seated
correctly and should not show leakage.

Step 5. If the problem involves slow or no filling, inspect the inlet screens at the hose connections for visible dirt or
sediment. Clean only the accessible screens using the procedure recommended by the manual; do not damage
or remove internal components.

Step 6. Reconnect the hoses securely, restore the water supply, and run a short test cycle. Observe whether
water enters normally.

Step 7. If the washer still has a fill problem after the external checks, the cause may involve the water valve,
pressure sensing system, wiring, or control board. These are service-level checks and should not be opened or
tested as a DIY repair.
When to escalate: If the problem remains after the safe external checks, or if the washer shows repeated electrical,
sensor, control, motor, valve, pump, or lock faults, stop user troubleshooting and arrange qualified service.
Samsung WA5471ABP/XAA — Leakage Problems
Page 4
